minor.issue: 'Six of seven studies that measured strength reported significant benefit from BFRT' turns within-group improvements into benefit attributable to BFRT. The source says BFRT was significantly better than controls in only 3 isokinetic investigations, controls also improved, and BFRT was not superior to high-resistance controls (Ferraz).
'Some studies reported quadriceps CSA gains' softens the source's 'Few benefits in quadriceps CSA were reported'.
Does not mention that only 4 studies did power analyses and only 2 reported effect sizes.
The 2019;11(1):69-83 details cannot be verified from the source, which is the 2018 online-first version.
'Limited support after ACL reconstruction' should note that one of the three ACL trials (Iversen) reported unsatisfactory results.

note: B separates within-group strength gains from the 3 studies showing superiority over controls and gives accurate search, quality and power-analysis details; A's practical guidance is good but its findings overstate how much of the strength benefit is attributable to BFRT.
